items.name: Cylinder block
items.what: The cast aluminium 90 degree V8 block that carries the cylinders and everything else on the engine.
items.why: It sets the bore and deck the whole engine is built around, and the 4.0 bore coating decides how you check a used engine.
items.location: Centre of the engine bay, front to rear along the car.
items.accessNotes: Bare blocks are not sold as a catalogue line; SNG lists only the fittings for it.

partNumbers.desc: Sealing washer for screw plug, qty 2

items.note: Factory guide gives 200 kg (441 lb) for the 4.0. JEC prints the 4.2 supercharged bore as 96 mm, a typo: Jaguar's 4.2 data gives 86 x 90.3 mm. Early cylinders are Nikasil coated; Wikipedia says affected engines were replaced and later ones use cast iron liners. The running-change date is in variants.json.

items.name: Bedplate
items.what: A structural aluminium casting bolted under the block that holds the crankshaft in place of separate main caps.
items.why: It carries the oil pump pickup, diverter valve where fitted, and the oil filter, as well as the main bearings. The joint to the block is sealed with beads of sealant, not a gasket.
items.location: Bottom of the block, between block and structural sump.
items.accessNotes: Two hollow dowels align it to the block. Iron inserts are cast into the main bearing supports.

items.name: Main bearing bolts
items.what: The set of long and short bolts that clamp the bedplate and crankshaft to the block.
items.why: Three lengths exist, so note which hole each came from when you strip the bottom end.
items.location: Inside the bedplate, reached from underneath once the sump is off.

partNumbers.desc: Main bearing bolt 114mm, to VIN A40153, qty 10
Main bearing bolt 114mm, from VIN A40154, qty 10

items.name: Crankshaft
items.what: The shaft that turns piston movement into rotation, with rolled fillets; stroke is 86 mm on the 4.0 and 90.3 mm on the 4.2, and the 4.2 crank is cast iron.
items.why: Its stroke is the difference between the two engine sizes, and the crank type changes at the engine number break that also changes the chain parts.
items.location: Bottom of the block, held by the bedplate.
items.accessNotes: Drives two chain sprockets through one key. The torsional damper retains both sprockets.

items.name: Main bearing shells
items.what: The graded upper and lower shells the crankshaft runs in; upper shells are grooved and lower shells plain.
items.why: They are graded from codes on the engine, so a rebuild reads crank and block grades first. Aluminium/tin material.
items.location: Between crank journals and the block and bedplate.
items.accessNotes: SNG sells them by grade through the sales desk, with no part numbers printed.

items.name: Crankshaft thrust washer
items.what: A pair of washers that control how far the crankshaft can move front to back.
items.why: Renewed on any bottom-end strip.
items.location: At one main bearing, either side of the journal.

items.name: Crankshaft front oil seal
items.what: The lip seal where the crank nose leaves the timing cover.
items.why: A leak here means pulling the damper, a job you combine with belt work.
items.location: In the timing cover, behind the damper.

items.name: Crankshaft rear oil seal
items.what: The lip seal at the rear of the crank behind the drive plate.
items.why: Getting to it means taking the gearbox off.
items.location: Rear of block and bedplate, behind the drive plate.

items.name: Crankshaft damper
items.what: The torsional vibration damper and pulley on the crank nose, which also retains the chain sprockets.
items.why: It is variant specific, so order by engine, induction and number break. Its bolt and split collet are separate lines.
items.location: Front of the engine, bottom centre.
items.accessNotes: Damper bolt AJ89909 and split collet AJ89854 are listed with it.

partNumbers.desc: 4.0 non supercharged, VIN 008243 to 042775, and A00083 to A30644 to engine 0108122359
4.0 non supercharged, later engines; catalogue prints the break as engine 010812230000

items.name: Drive plate
items.what: The thin plate on the rear of the crank that carries the starter ring and bolts to the torque converter.
items.why: The engine speed sensor reads a timing disc spot welded to its front face, so a damaged plate can show up as a sensor fault.
items.location: Between the engine and the gearbox bell housing.
items.accessNotes: Gearbox off. Bolt type and quantity change at VIN 031303. Drive plate cover is C2C10161.

partNumbers.desc: Drive plate, 4.0 A00083 to A30644 and all 4.2
Bolt, plate to crank, to VIN 031302, qty 8
Bolt, plate to crank, from VIN 031303, qty 8
Setscrew, torque converter, A30645 to A36272, qty 3
Setscrew, torque converter, from A36273, qty 3

items.name: Piston
items.what: The open-skirt piston running in each 86 mm bore, with two compression rings and one oil ring.
items.why: Compression differs a lot by engine, from about 9:1 supercharged to about 11:1 on the 4.2 NA, so pistons are not interchangeable across variants.
items.accessNotes: SNG lists pistons at qty 8 through the sales desk with no number printed.
items.note: JEC prints 11.1:1 for the 4.2 NA and 9:1 for the 4.2 SC; Jaguar handbook data shows 11.0:1 and 9.1:1. Compression height and pin diameter not found.

items.name: Piston ring kit
items.what: The set of two compression rings and one oil control ring per piston.
items.why: 4.0 kits split at an engine number, and the break is different for supercharged and non supercharged.

partNumbers.desc: 4.0 supercharged to engine 0008180853; 4.0 NA to engine 0008180924
4.0 supercharged from engine 0008180854; 4.0 NA from engine 0008180925

items.name: Piston pin circlip
items.what: The clip that keeps the gudgeon pin in the piston.
items.why: Two per piston, and the type differs by engine and VIN.
items.location: Each end of the piston pin.

partNumbers.desc: 4.0; also 4.2 NA from VIN A40154, qty 2
4.2 NA to VIN A40153 and 4.2 supercharged, qty 2

items.name: Connecting rod
items.what: The sinter-forged steel rod linking piston to crank, with a cap split by fracturing.
items.why: Each cap fits only its own rod because the broken faces interlock, and the cylinder position is etched at the joint. Never mix them.
items.location: Between each piston and the crank.
items.accessNotes: Check the etched cylinder marks before separating any cap.

partNumbers.desc: Connecting rod assembly, 4.2 non supercharged, qty 8

items.name: Connecting rod bolt
items.what: The two bolts that clamp each big-end cap.
items.why: Listed per rod, and different for 4.0 and 4.2.

items.name: Big end bearing shells
items.what: The colour-graded shells each rod runs in on the crank.
items.why: Blue, green and yellow grades exist, so match the grade or you get the wrong clearance.

items.name: Cylinder head
items.what: The aluminium four-valve head on each bank, with twin cams, one spark plug per cylinder and a lifting eye cast in the front.
items.why: Heads are bank specific. A used-head swap also has to match tappets.
items.location: Top of each cylinder bank. A-bank is the right side, B-bank the left.
items.accessNotes: 20 bolts M10 x 175mm. Two hollow dowels align each head. Rear lifting eyes are bolt-on tools, not part of the head.

partNumbers.desc: LH, B-bank, 4.0 and 4.2, without valves, use with tappets AJ83694
RH, A-bank, 4.0 and 4.2, without valves, use with tappets AJ83694

items.note: The 2013 catalogue prints the first RH head number as 2C2A1012 and the later one as C2A1012; the leading 2 reads as a misprint.

items.name: Cylinder head gasket
items.what: The silicon-beaded composite gasket with metal eyelets that seals each head to the block.
items.why: Each bank has its own gasket, and 4.0 numbers change at an engine break.

items.name: Cylinder head bolt
items.what: The deep-seated bolts that hold each head to the block.
items.why: Deep seating is there to reduce distortion, so do not substitute generic bolts.

partNumbers.desc: Cylinder head bolt M10 x 175mm, qty 20

items.name: Inlet camshaft
items.what: The chilled cast iron cam on each bank that opens the inlet valves and, on VVT engines, carries the timing unit.
items.why: Numbers differ by bank, induction and VIN, and the sprocket drive is by friction, not a key.
items.location: Top of each head, inner side.
items.accessNotes: Five aluminium caps retain each cam, numbered 0 to 4 on the inlet cam. A flat near the front lets you lock it for timing. Sprockets are non-keyed friction fits.

partNumbers.desc: RH, A-bank, 4.0 supercharged VIN 031303 to A30644
RH, A-bank, 4.0 NA VIN 031303 to A30644

items.name: Exhaust camshaft
items.what: The chilled cast iron cam on each bank that opens the exhaust valves, driven by the secondary chain.
items.why: Needed to model the top end; no catalogue number was found.
items.location: Top of each head, outer side.
items.accessNotes: Five aluminium caps, numbered 5 to 9. A flat near the front lets you lock it for timing.

items.name: Tappet
items.what: The solid aluminium alloy valve lifter between cam lobe and valve.
items.why: Type changes at VIN 031303 and A30645, and a replacement head is paired with a specific tappet.
items.location: In the head, under each lobe.

items.name: Tappet adjustment shim
items.what: The steel shim in the top of each lifter that sets valve clearance.
items.why: Clearance is set by swapping shims. Cold clearance is 0.18 to 0.22 mm inlet and 0.23 to 0.27 mm exhaust.
items.note: The catalogue lists about 50 sizes between AJ84884 and AJ84937; only the two ends and one mid value are stored here. Numbers do not run strictly in sequence, so look up the size you need.

items.name: Inlet valve
items.what: The poppet valve that lets air and fuel in, two per cylinder, with a 35 mm head.
items.why: 16 fitted. All valves use a thin 5 mm stem, and stem seals are built into the spring seats.

partNumbers.desc: Inlet valve, qty 16; Rimmer shows it cross-references nca2533ba

items.name: Exhaust valve
items.what: The poppet valve that lets burnt gas out, two per cylinder, with a 31 mm head.
items.why: 16 fitted. Same 5 mm stem as the inlet.

items.name: Valve spring
items.what: The coil spring that closes each valve.
items.why: Single springs on both valves. Three part numbers across production, split by VIN. Lighter tappets and modified springs came with later engines.
items.location: Around each valve stem under the tappet.

items.name: Valve seat
items.what: The hard insert in the head that each valve closes against.
items.why: Separate inlet and exhaust numbers exist for head repair.

items.name: Camshaft cover
items.what: The composite cover over each pair of cams, vinyl ester on the 4.0 and thermoplastic on the 4.2, carrying the breather outlets.
items.why: Plastic covers with silicone in-groove gaskets. A-bank has the full-load breather and B-bank the part-load breather.
items.accessNotes: Coil cover comes off first. Fasteners, grommets and studs are listed separately and differ between 4.0 and 4.2.

partNumbers.desc: 4.0 VVT LH to VIN 031202; also 4.0 non VVT LH
4.0 VVT RH with VVT access hole

items.note: Catalogue prints the first 4.0 VVT LH break as VIN 031202 and most other breaks as 031302; 031202 reads as a misprint.

items.name: Camshaft cover gasket
items.what: The silicone in-groove gasket between cam cover and head.
items.why: A leak source you can reach without major strip. Numbers change at an engine break.

partNumbers.desc: Cam cover centre seal, engine 9810290000 on, qty 4

items.name: Spark plug boss seal
items.what: The seal round each spark plug well in the cam cover.
items.why: Early 4.0 engines use a joined seal per bank, later ones an individual seal per cylinder, so count before you order.
items.location: In each cam cover at the plug tube.

items.name: Oil filler cap
items.what: The screw cap on the B-bank cam cover.
items.why: Same number for 4.0 and 4.2; on the 4.2 it sits on a separate filler pipe.

items.name: Timing cover
items.what: The cover over the chain drive at the front of the engine, holding the front crank seal.
items.why: Coming off it is the gateway to all tensioner and chain work. Variant specific.
items.accessNotes: 24 bolts JFB10607B and 3 dowels NCC1236AA.
items.note: The 4.2 cover numbers appear in the catalogue as item 7 with no noun; the diagram places them as the timing cover.

items.name: Primary timing chain
items.what: The chain on each bank from the crank to the inlet cam unit, single row on the 4.0 and multi row on the 4.2.
items.why: Early and later engines take different numbers, so read the engine number first.
items.location: Behind the timing cover, one per bank.
items.accessNotes: Runs on a tensioner blade and a guide. Timing cover must be off.
items.note: Moss sells AJ8-2289 as the lower or primary chain for later 4.0 and 4.2 from engine 0108122360, a Moss item code. SNG lists EAZ1269 with no split. Pitch not found: one seller page mentions 6.35 mm and another 8.0 mm, neither tied to this part.

items.name: Secondary timing chain
items.what: The single-row chain on each bank from the inlet cam unit across to the exhaust cam.
items.why: Paired with the secondary tensioner, the classic failure area on these engines.
items.location: At the top of each head, behind the timing cover.

items.name: Primary chain tensioner
items.what: The oil-pressure hydraulic plunger that loads the primary chain through its blade.
items.why: Rimmer lists AJ82325 as the metal lower tensioner in its upgrade kit. Early plastic-bodied parts are the known weakness.
items.location: Lower front of the engine, behind the timing cover.
items.accessNotes: Catalogue fixes it with bolts C2Z2642 to VIN A30644 and JFB10607B after. Blanking plate NCA2002BD applies to VIN A30644.

partNumbers.desc: Blanking plate, to VIN A30644, qty 2

items.name: Secondary chain tensioner
items.what: The oil-pressure hydraulic tensioner that loads each secondary chain, bank specific.
items.why: SNG says original tensioners can fail early, and Moss warns worn plastic ones can let a chain jump teeth. JCNA says the part was redesigned three times.
items.location: Top front of each head, between the cams.
items.accessNotes: Moss says two JFB10607B bolts per tensioner when converting from plastic. Rimmer lists JFB10607E x 4. One forum owner found the metal body needs shorter bolts.
items.note: Bolt numbers disagree between Moss and Rimmer, so check bolt length against your head before final tightening.

items.name: Chain tensioner blade
items.what: The curved sliding blade the primary tensioner pushes on.
items.why: Number changes at the engine break. Moss says two per engine.
items.accessNotes: Pivots on bolt NCA2028AA for the 4.0 and AJ82382 for the 4.2, with bush AJ86824.

partNumbers.desc: From engine 0108130000, qty 2; Moss lists it for later 4.0 and 4.2, from engine 0108122360

items.name: Primary chain guide
items.what: The fixed guide on the tight side of each primary chain.
items.why: Renewed with chains.

items.name: Crankshaft sprocket
items.what: One of the two sprockets on the crank nose, keyed and held by the damper.
items.why: Two per engine, one per bank.

items.name: Exhaust camshaft sprocket
items.what: The sprocket on each exhaust cam, driven by the secondary chain.
items.why: Non-keyed friction fit, so its spacer and bolt matter.

partNumbers.desc: Socket bolt M12 x 63mm, to engine 0108122359
Socket bolt M12 x 44mm, from engine 0108130000

items.name: Inlet camshaft sprocket
items.what: The inlet cam sprocket fitted on supercharged engines, which have no VVT unit on the 4.0.
items.why: Takes the place of the VVT unit on the 4.0 supercharged engine.

partNumbers.desc: 4.0 supercharged from engine 0108130000, and 4.2 supercharged, qty 2

items.note: Wikipedia says the supercharged AJ27S has no VVT and the 4.2 AJ34 adds it, yet SNG lists both sprockets and VVT units for 4.2; confirm on the car.

items.name: Variable valve timing unit
items.what: The oil-operated unit on the front of each inlet cam that shifts cam timing, also the top sprocket for both chains.
items.why: Choice depends on VIN and engine size. The unit is a non-keyed friction fit on the cam.
items.accessNotes: Bolts M12 x 38mm AJ83900, or NCA2656AB on early engines.
items.note: JTIS says VVT is on naturally aspirated 4.0 engines only. The 2003 JTIS text says continuous VCT on 4.2 inlet cams. SNG lists a 4.2 unit AJ89778.

items.name: VVT solenoid valve
items.what: The electrically driven oil valve that controls each VVT unit.
items.why: One per bank, same number for all listed years.
items.location: On the VVT module carrier at the front of each head.

items.name: VVT module carrier
items.what: The bracket assembly on the front of each head that carries the VVT oil feed and tensioner mounting.
items.why: Contains a small oil filter, which is easy to forget on a chain job.

partNumbers.desc: 4.0 LH later engines; catalogue prints from engine 010810000

items.name: Timing chain kit
items.what: A prepared set of chains and latest-type tensioners, sold ready to fit.
items.why: Usually cheaper and safer than buying each item. SNG sells three grades and British Parts sells upgrade kits with metal-backed guides.

partNumbers.desc: OE specification tensioners, copy chains, SNG number
Copy tensioners and chains, no gaskets or seals, SNG number
Upgrade kit, 4.0 V8 1996 to 2000, British Parts number
Kit, XK8 and XKR 4.0 V8 2001 on, from engine number 010813000, British Parts number

items.name: Oil filter
items.what: The spin-on filter on the engine oil circuit.
items.why: A basic service part. 4.0 and 4.2 numbers are different.
items.location: On the oil filter adaptor on the structural sump.

items.name: Oil filter adaptor
items.what: The block the filter threads onto.
items.why: Oil cooler type sumps also carry a diverter valve near here.

items.name: Oil pump
items.what: The pump on the crank nose that feeds the engine, the chain tensioners and VVT with oil.
items.why: Kit differs before and after engine 0108122359.
items.location: On the crankshaft at the front of the engine.

items.name: Oil pickup pipe
items.what: The moulded composite pickup, with a mesh screen, that draws oil from the sump pan.
items.why: Its castellated inlet keeps oil flowing even if the pan is dented. A blocked screen starves the engine.

partNumbers.desc: Oil pickup pipe, 4.2; catalogue prints from VIN A302645
Suction pipe oil seal, to engine 0108122359

items.name: Windage tray
items.what: A plate that keeps oil in the pan away from the spinning crank.
items.why: It is in the way of anything inside the sump.
items.location: Under the crank, above the sump pan.
items.accessNotes: 8 M5 screws FA105101J, 16 M8 bolts JFB10808E in the same diagram.

items.name: Structural sump
items.what: The structural sump bolted under the bedplate.
items.why: Two versions exist depending on whether the car has an engine oil cooler.
items.accessNotes: Has a torque converter access opening.

items.name: Sump pan
items.what: The shallow pressed pan that closes the bottom of the structural sump and holds the oil.
items.why: Same pan for 4.0 and 4.2.
items.accessNotes: 18 flange screws M6 x 12mm: JZS100105 to VIN 042775, JZH100059 from A00083.

partNumbers.desc: Flange screw M6 x 12mm, to VIN 042775, qty 18
Flange screw M6 x 12mm, from VIN A00083, qty 18

items.name: Sump drain plug
items.what: The plug and washer used to drain the engine oil.
items.why: Fit a new washer at every oil change.

partNumbers.desc: Drain plug and washer; also sealing washer to VIN 042775

items.name: Engine oil dipstick and tube
items.what: The dipstick and the tube it runs in.
items.why: Three dipstick numbers by VIN, and using the wrong one misreads the oil level.

items.name: Engine oil cooler
items.what: A small radiator for engine oil, fitted on some variants.
items.why: Check whether your car has one; sump, hoses and radiator details follow from it.

partNumbers.desc: From engine 0108130000; also 4.2 NA to VIN A40264 printed as MJF77440AA

items.note: The catalogue prints MJF77440AA once and MJF7440AA once; the double 7 reads as a misprint.

items.name: Oil pressure switch
items.what: The switch that lights the oil warning.
items.why: A cheap part, and the first thing to check when the warning comes on with good measured pressure.
items.location: On the engine; the sensor diagram shows it as a black unit.

items.name: Crankcase breather
items.what: The hoses and valve that take crankcase gases back to the intake.
items.why: Part-load and full-load paths are separate, with oil separators under the cam cover outlets. JTIS links a blocked part-load breather to detonation.
items.location: From the cam covers to the intake.

items.name: Block valley cover
items.what: The cover over the vee of the block under the intake.
items.why: Comes into view when the intake or supercharger is off.
items.location: In the vee of the engine.

items.name: Engine gasket sets
items.what: Boxed gasket sets for the top and bottom of the engine.
items.why: Saves hunting single gaskets. Top sets are sold for the 4.0, 4.2 through the sales desk.

items.name: Engine cover
items.what: The trim cover or pair of covers on top of the engine.
items.why: First thing off on most under-bonnet jobs.

items.name: Hydraulic engine mounting
items.what: The fluid-filled mount that carries each side of the engine on the front crossbeam.
items.why: Early and late types supersede to one number. Two per car.
items.location: Between the engine brackets and the front crossbeam.

partNumbers.desc: Hydraulic engine mounting, supersedes early type, qty 2

items.note: The catalogue also prints MNC7500AB against the engine mounting heat shield line, which reads as a misprint, so the heat shield number stays unset.

items.name: Rear engine mounting
items.what: The rear mount that holds the back of the engine and gearbox to the body, with its bracket.
items.why: Many numbers by VIN.
items.location: Under the gearbox tail, in the tunnel.

partNumbers.desc: Mounting bracket, 4.0 NA VIN 014500 to A30644

items.name: Accessory drive belt
items.what: The seven-ribbed belt that drives the front accessories.
items.why: Number changes with VIN and induction. The tensioner has a wear indicator, so read it before buying.

items.name: Accessory belt tensioner
items.what: The automatic sprung tensioner on the accessory belt, with a belt wear indicator.
items.why: Five numbers by VIN. Check it when the belt is off.

items.name: Accessory belt idler pulley
items.what: The plain pulley that routes the accessory belt.
items.why: Check bearing noise with the belt off.

partNumbers.desc: Alternator idler pulley, from VIN A30645

items.name: Air cleaner box
items.what: A plastic base and cover that clamp the filter, held by five over-centre clips.
items.why: Numbers split by engine, and it opens with 5 clamps.
items.location: On a bracket on the inner wing, mounted in grommets.
items.accessNotes: 5 clamps NAB3511AA.

partNumbers.desc: To VIN 042775, and 4.0 supercharged A00083 to A30644

items.name: Air filter element
items.what: The flat panel filter in the air box.
items.why: A basic service part. SNG lists a different number for the 4.2 NA.
items.note: Moss lists NJA3558AA for XK8 and XKR 4.0 and 4.2 with no split. SNG lists XR823351 for the 4.2 NA. Size from Mann C31130 and Wix WA6653, which agree.

items.name: Air flow sensor
items.what: The combined air flow and intake temperature sensor on the air cleaner cover.
items.why: Numbers split by engine, induction and VIN. Jaguar Club lists a DIY clean guide, so cleaning is a recognised first step.
items.location: Between air cleaner and throttle duct.

items.name: Inlet air pipe
items.what: The duct from air box or air flow sensor to the throttle.
items.why: Split by induction and VIN; check its seals for air leaks.
items.location: Top front of the engine bay.

items.name: Throttle body
items.what: The electronically controlled throttle at the mouth of the intake; early cars have a cable as well.
items.why: Several types. Factory guide calls electronic throttle a key new feature of the engine.

items.name: Inlet manifold
items.what: The manifold that shares intake air among the cylinders on non supercharged engines.
items.why: Comes off for almost any job in the vee.
items.location: In the vee of the engine.
items.accessNotes: Bolts include AJ81194 M8 x 112mm qty 9, and AJ88674 M6 x 55mm qty 11 on the 4.2.

items.name: Inlet manifold seal
items.what: The port seals and gaskets that seal the manifold to the heads.
items.why: An air leak here gives lean codes and rough idle.

partNumbers.desc: Inlet manifold seal, to VIN 031302, qty 8
Inlet manifold seal, from VIN 031303, qty 8
Inlet manifold gasket, 4.2, VIN A30645 to A36873, qty 2
Inlet manifold gasket, 4.2, from VIN A36874, qty 2

items.name: Manifold absolute pressure sensor
items.what: The sensor that reads pressure in the intake.
items.why: Number changes with VIN and is shared across engines. 2-hole fixing.
items.location: On the intake elbow or manifold.

partNumbers.desc: 2 hole fixing, to VIN A24195 in one table and to A43927 in another
From VIN A24196 in one table and from A43928 in another

items.note: The VIN break differs between the engine sensors page and the bypass valve page of the same catalogue; check your sensor first.

items.name: Intake air temperature sensor
items.what: The sensor that reports charge air temperature.
items.why: Separate number on supercharged cars.
items.location: In the intake on supercharged cars.

items.name: Supercharger
items.what: The belt-driven Eaton M112 Roots blower that forces air into the XKR engine.
items.why: Delivers the XKR power. Spins at 1.9 times engine speed with about 11.9 psi boost.
items.location: In the vee of the engine.
items.accessNotes: Bracket NCC7708AB, flange bolts JDE4411 and 4 dowels EAZ2159.

items.name: Supercharger drive belt
items.what: The separate belt that drives the blower from the crank.
items.why: Its own part number and tensioner, so check it at every belt service.
items.location: Front of the engine, with the blower drive.

partNumbers.desc: VIN A30645 to A41575; catalogue prints A415575
From VIN A41576; catalogue prints A415576
Drive belt in the NCC7753AD idler replacement kit

items.note: A415575 has an extra digit. The bolt in the same diagram breaks at VIN 41575/41576, used here.

items.name: Supercharger belt tensioner
items.what: The tensioner on the blower drive belt.
items.why: Four numbers by VIN.

partNumbers.desc: Tensioner and idler bracket in the NCC7753AD replacement kit

items.name: Supercharger idler pulley
items.what: The idler in the blower belt drive.
items.why: NCC7753AD is unavailable, so early cars move to a kit of bracket, tensioner, pulley and belt.

partNumbers.desc: To VIN A30644, listed as unavailable

items.name: Charge air intercooler
items.what: The twin air-to-liquid coolers that sit in the outlet path of the supercharger.
items.why: Their seals and clamp plates are the service items. They run on their own water circuit.
items.location: One per bank, clamped between the supercharger outlet and the head side of the intake.

partNumbers.desc: Clamp plate, LH B-bank, from engine 9811240000
Clamp plate, LH B-bank, to engine 9811230000

items.name: Intercooler radiator
items.what: The small radiator that sheds heat from the intercooler water circuit.
items.why: SNG calls it the radiator in the intercooler list; it has its own brackets.
items.location: Front of the car, with its own brackets.

items.name: Supercharger coolant pump
items.what: The electric pump that moves water through the intercooler circuit.
items.why: If it stops, charge air heats up quickly. Same pump across the list.
items.location: On a bracket with hoses to the intercooler circuit.

items.name: Supercharger induction elbow
items.what: The elbow that takes air from the throttle into the intake or the supercharger.
items.why: Different castings by engine. On NA cars it feeds the intake manifold; on supercharged cars the blower.

items.name: Supercharger outlet elbow
items.what: The casting that takes pressurised air from the blower to the intercoolers.
items.why: Same number on the 4.0 and 4.2 lists.

items.name: Supercharger bypass valve
items.what: The vacuum-actuated valve that lets the blower recirculate air at light load.
items.why: Vacuum drives it, so check the hoses on any boost complaint.

items.name: EGR valve
items.what: The valve that lets a metered amount of exhaust back into the intake.
items.why: Same number on the lists for 4.0 supercharged and 4.2.
items.location: On the engine with a pipe from the exhaust side.

items.name: Fuel tank
items.what: The 75 litre tank, 70 litres shown from E to F and 5 litres below E.
items.why: Several tank numbers by VIN. Straps and pads are separate lines.
items.location: In the boot, over the rear suspension, with fuel lines down the left underside of the car.
items.accessNotes: Two straps NJA6045BF and flanged screws C2Z1856.

partNumbers.desc: Catalogue prints VIN A3660 to A30644

items.note: One seller gives 75.3 L. A30659 and A3660 in the catalogue read as neighbouring breaks with a dropped digit.

items.name: Fuel pump
items.what: The in-tank pump assembly that feeds the fuel rail.
items.why: Numbers split at VIN A30645 by induction.

partNumbers.desc: Pump assembly, from VIN A30645, supercharged
Pump assembly, from VIN A30645, NA

items.name: Fuel level sender
items.what: The tank unit that reports fuel level.
items.why: Sealing and locking rings are separate lines, and renew them.

items.name: Fuel filter
items.what: The in-line filter in the fuel feed.
items.why: Service item. Two O-rings XR829166 are listed with it.
items.location: In a bracket on the fuel line; SNG shows it with bracket NJA6086AC.

items.name: Fuel filler and cap
items.what: The filler neck, cap and drain.
items.why: Has a separate drain tube and drain filter, so check they are clear.

items.name: Fuel injector
items.what: The electrically operated nozzle that sprays fuel at each inlet port.
items.why: 8 fitted, type by engine and VIN. Each has two O-rings on the 4.2.
items.location: In the fuel rail, at each inlet port.
items.note: The 4.2 page shows two rails: one NA, one supercharged. The text extraction does not show which injector matches which rail.

items.name: Fuel rail
items.what: The pipe that feeds all the injectors.
items.why: Sensor and regulator hang off it.

items.name: Fuel pressure regulator
items.what: The regulator on the rail that holds fuel pressure steady.
items.why: Sold as a kit.

items.name: Fuel pressure sensor
items.what: The sensor that reports fuel pressure.
items.why: Tank sensor on earlier cars, rail sensor on the 4.2.
items.location: At the tank on the 4.0 list, on the fuel rail on the 4.2.

items.name: Fuel feed and return pipes
items.what: The fixed pipes running under the car from tank to engine.
items.why: Age and clip corrosion matter on an older car. Split by VIN.

items.name: Evaporative loss hoses
items.what: The vapour pipes and purge hoses that stop tank fumes escaping.
items.why: A leak here can set an emissions code. Numbers split by VIN.
items.location: Around the tank and along the underside.

items.name: Accelerator cable and pedal
items.what: The pedal assembly and the cable that links it to the throttle.
items.why: RHD and LHD have different numbers. 4.2 adds a pedal position sensor.

partNumbers.desc: Pedal sub-assembly, RHD, to VIN A30644
Pedal sub-assembly, RHD, from VIN A30645

items.name: Spark plug
items.what: One 14 mm spark plug per cylinder, seated down the centre of the head.
items.why: A core service part. Numbers split by VIN, and supercharged 4.0 cars take their own plug.
items.location: Under the on-plug coils, in the centre of each cam cover.
items.accessNotes: Lift the coil cover (screws AJ84085) and coils first.

partNumbers.desc: 4.0 from VIN 031303 and all 4.2; eBay lists it as an NGK SK16PR-L11 equivalent
NGK/Denso style interchange shown in one listing
NGK platinum plug named in the 1996 guide for the 4.0
NGK plug in the factory vehicle data table, 4.0 NA

items.note: Factory gap is 1.0 mm in one document and 1.0 to 1.1 mm in another.

items.name: On-plug ignition coil
items.what: The individual coil sitting on top of each spark plug.
items.why: 8 fitted. 2-pin and 4-pin 4.0 types are not interchangeable.
items.location: On each plug in the cam covers.
items.accessNotes: Held by hexagon flange screw AJ84085 (4.0) or AJ85385 and AJ88474 (4.2).
items.note: Catalogue says 2-pin and 4-pin but gives no VIN split for the 4.0. Check the connector on your car.

items.name: On-plug coil cover
items.what: The plastic cover over the coils on each bank.
items.why: Only comes off with 24 small screws on the 4.0, so have a magnetic tray ready.
items.accessNotes: Screw AJ84085, qty 24.

items.name: Ignition power module
items.what: The power stage that switches the coils on earlier cars.
items.why: To VIN A30644 only.

partNumbers.desc: Ignition power module, to VIN A30644, qty 2

items.name: Crankshaft position sensor
items.what: The sensor that reads the timing disc on the drive plate to give engine speed.
items.why: Without it the engine will not run. Early and later numbers.
items.location: Listed as the sump position in the sensor diagram, near the drive plate.

items.name: Camshaft position sensor
items.what: The sensor on each bank that reads cam position.
items.why: Bank specific.

items.name: Knock sensor
items.what: The sensor bolted to the block that hears detonation.
items.why: Two fitted. Early and later types use different studs.
items.location: In the vee of the block; stud fixed.

partNumbers.desc: Supercharged to VIN 042775, NA to VIN 031302, qty 2
Supercharged from A00083, NA from VIN 031303, qty 2
Knock sensor stud, to VIN A24195, qty 2
Knock sensor stud, from VIN A24196, qty 2

items.name: Radiator
items.what: The main radiator, with a plate-type transmission oil cooler built into its outlet tank.
items.why: Number changes at VIN A30645. Sizes differ, so compare core depth before buying.
items.location: Front of the car, in radiator mounting panel MJA4180AD, with cooling fans behind it.
items.accessNotes: Top and lower mounting bushes MJA4243AB and MJA4242CB, two of each.

partNumbers.desc: Nissens aftermarket radiator for XK8 and XKR

items.note: 670 x 433 x 34 mm is from Rimmer for C2N4579 and from a Nissens 66701 listing. A separate listing for an MJB4190BC match gives 664 x 428 x 26 mm with an oil cooler. Rimmer lists C2N4579 as no longer available.

items.name: Expansion tank
items.what: The pressurised coolant reservoir, the system filling point, with its low level sensor and a 1 bar cap.
items.why: Coolant should sit level with the bottom of the filler neck.
items.location: Left front firewall extension in the engine bay.

partNumbers.desc: Coolant reservoir, catalogue prints from VIN A36045

items.note: A36045 may be a misprint for A30645; the line above breaks at A30644.

items.name: Atmospheric recovery bottle
items.what: The atmospheric catchment tank that takes pressure relief from the reservoir cap.
items.why: Has its own cap, seal and overflow pipe.

items.name: Thermostat
items.what: The heat-sensitive valve that controls when coolant goes to the radiator.
items.why: A common renewal, and seller listings disagree on opening temperature, so confirm yours.
items.location: In the thermostat housing, under the thermostat cover.
items.accessNotes: Thermostat cover held by 3 bolts AJ89714, seal NCA2246BA.

partNumbers.desc: Thermostat, supercharged list; Motorad shows it interchanging with AJ86484

items.note: Opening temperature: TRE listings say 87 C. Valeo 820548 listing says 81 C for the same cross-references. Neither is a Jaguar figure.

items.name: Thermostat housing
items.what: The housing that carries the thermostat and joins the coolant hoses.
items.why: On the 4.0 NA it is thin plastic and can crack when a top hose is disturbed. SNG sells an aluminium replacement with O-rings.
items.accessNotes: Cap NCA2270AC, cover NCA2277AA, bolts C2Z1354 qty 8, housing seal NCA2269CA.
items.note: The page shows NA and supercharged diagrams with one item list, so the AJ87639 grouping is inferred. SNG calls the NA 4.0 housing plastic. An eBay listing for AJ82217 calls its part aluminium, which is the upgrade version; Moss sells it as AJ8-2217/1. Buy by material, not number alone.

items.name: Coolant outlet pipe
items.what: The outlet pipe that links the two banks and carries the temperature sensor.
items.why: Comes off with the thermostat housing. Sits on seals C2C11477.
items.location: Front of the engine across the banks.

items.name: Coolant temperature sensor
items.what: The sensor that tells the ECM engine coolant temperature.
items.why: Drives gauge and fuelling; early check on running problems.

partNumbers.desc: Temperature sensor M18 thread, sensors page
Temperature sensor M18 thread, sensors page, second table

items.name: Water pump
items.what: The belt-driven pump that moves coolant through the engine.
items.why: Same pump across the catalogue. Gasket comes in two thicknesses, so fit the correct one.
items.accessNotes: 5 flange bolts AJ88674. O-rings 55 mm KSR634001 and 70 mm KSE169530.

items.name: Water pump pulley
items.what: The pulley that drives the water pump from the accessory belt.
items.why: Three numbers by VIN.

items.name: Radiator top hose
items.what: The upper hose between engine and radiator.
items.why: Disturbing it is how plastic housings crack on the 4.0 NA, so ease it off carefully. Hose ends have orientation marks and spring clamps.
items.location: Top of radiator to thermostat housing.

items.name: Radiator bottom hose
items.what: The lower hose between radiator and water pump side of the engine.
items.why: Drain point area on most jobs.

items.name: Coolant bypass hose
items.what: The short hose that lets coolant circulate with the thermostat closed.
items.why: Short, tucked in and easy to forget.

items.name: Fan and cowl assembly
items.what: Two electric fans in a plastic cowl on the back of the radiator, one 305 mm and one 325 mm.
items.why: Sold as an assembly. Run in slow or fast mode, switched by the ECM through a fan control module.

items.name: Block heater
items.what: An optional electric heater in a block core position.
items.why: Market option, 110 V and 220 V versions.

items.name: Exhaust manifold
items.what: The cast manifold on each head that gathers exhaust into the downpipe.
items.why: Bank specific, with EGR and non-EGR versions on the A-bank. The 4.2 manifolds are stainless steel.
items.accessNotes: 16 bolts and 16 spacers, split by VIN.

partNumbers.desc: 4.0 LH B-bank, non EGR and EGR
4.0 RH A-bank, non EGR, from engine 9809020000
Manifold bolt to VIN A46332, qty 16
Manifold bolt from VIN A46333, qty 16

items.name: Exhaust downpipe and catalyst
items.what: The downpipe with the catalytic converter built in, one per bank.
items.why: 4.2 numbers are in the catalogue; 4.0 downpipes are see salesman.
items.location: From each manifold down to the underfloor pipes.
items.accessNotes: Four studs fix the top flange to the manifold, with a gasket. Two nuts and bolts fix the lower end to a bracket on the engine. On a 4.0 the bottom slides into the front silencer under a clamp. On a 4.2 it is a flange with nuts and a gasket.

items.name: Heated oxygen sensor, upstream
items.what: The sensor ahead of each catalyst that controls fuel mixture.
items.why: Grey sensor on the 4.0. Fault codes for fuel trim lead here.
items.location: Upper threaded boss of each downpipe, before the catalyst.

partNumbers.desc: 4.0 supercharged, and 4.0 NA to VIN 031302, grey, qty 2

items.name: Heated oxygen sensor, downstream
items.what: The sensor after each catalyst that monitors catalyst health.
items.why: Black sensor on the 4.0. Market differences for USA and Canada.
items.location: Lower threaded boss of each downpipe, after the catalyst.

partNumbers.desc: USA and Canada, non heated, qty 2

items.name: Front exhaust silencer
items.what: The silencer section after the catalysts in the front system.
items.why: Number by engine and induction; held by 52.4 mm clamps.

items.name: Intermediate exhaust silencer
items.what: The middle silencers leading to the rear boxes.
items.why: Left and right are separate parts.

items.name: Rear silencer
items.what: The rear silencer box on each side.
items.why: Many numbers. SNG also lists a Bell sports kit as an upgrade.
items.location: Rear of the car under the bumper.

partNumbers.desc: RH 4.0 NA from VIN A11051, also 4.2 NA
LH 4.0 NA from VIN A11051, also 4.2 NA
Bell sports exhaust kit, XK8 and XKR

items.name: Tailpipe finisher
items.what: The bright trim at the end of each rear silencer on the 4.2.
items.why: Cosmetic, easy to fit, VIN dependent.

partNumbers.desc: Non supercharged, from VIN A40265, qty 2

items.name: Exhaust manifold heatshield
items.what: The thin metal shield around each manifold on the 4.2 supercharged.
items.why: Rattles when fixings loosen.

items.name: Automatic gearbox
items.what: The automatic transmission: ZF 5HP24 on the 4.0, Mercedes W5A580 on the 4.0 supercharged, ZF 6HP26 on 4.2 cars.
items.why: Which box you have decides fluid, filter and procedure. Exchange numbers are by VIN.
items.location: Behind the engine in the transmission tunnel.
items.accessNotes: Bell housing bolts M10 x 40mm qty 16.

partNumbers.desc: Exchange, 4.2 supercharged, printed from VIN A26998 to A41779
Exchange, 4.2 NA, printed from VIN A26998 to A41779

items.note: A26998 reads as a misprint for A36998: a line above stops at A36997 and the module table breaks at A36998. 95.8 kg is the ZF 5HP24 with torque converter.

items.name: Torque converter
items.what: The fluid coupling between drive plate and gearbox.
items.why: Separate numbers for each gearbox. Three setscrews reach it through the sump access.

items.name: Gearbox sump pan and filter
items.what: The pan under the gearbox that holds fluid, plus the gasket and filter behind it.
items.why: Every gearbox has different parts. 4.2 pan C2C38963 needs a separate check for filter arrangement.
items.note: Numbers grouped from the diagram labels. The 4.0 NA and supercharged groups are inferred from the two sets of items on the page, so verify against the pan on your car.

items.name: Gearbox control valve body
items.what: The hydraulic brain of the box; on the 4.2 it is a mechatronic unit with the control module built in.
items.why: Solenoids and pressure regulators are listed singly on 4.0 cars, so a repair may be cheaper than an exchange.
items.location: Inside the gearbox above the sump.

partNumbers.desc: Mechatronic unit, 4.2 to VIN A36997 SC and A31733 NA

items.name: Gear control cable
items.what: The cable from the J-gate to the gearbox selector.
items.why: Separate 4.0 supercharged, 4.0 NA and 4.2 numbers.

items.name: Gearbox oil cooler pipes
items.what: The pipes that carry fluid to the plate cooler in the radiator outlet tank.
items.why: A weeping joint here looks like an engine leak.
items.location: Along the engine bay to the gearbox.

items.name: Gearbox filler and level plugs
items.what: The plugs for checking and filling fluid on the sealed boxes.
items.why: Needed for any fluid level check.

items.name: Gearbox output shaft seal
items.what: The seal at the back of the gearbox where the output flange exits.
items.why: Leaks here drip near the propshaft coupling.

items.name: Gearbox speed transducer
items.what: The sensor that reports gearbox speed.
items.why: Feeds the gearbox control module.

items.name: Gearbox sump heatshield
items.what: Left and right shields protecting the sump from exhaust heat.
items.why: Hard to refit if a fixing rots out.

items.name: Propeller shaft
items.what: The one-piece aluminium shaft with a Jurid coupling, sliding joint and Hookes joint on the XK8; the XKR uses a two-piece shaft.
items.why: Numbers by engine. It joins through a flexible coupling.
items.location: Down the tunnel under the car.

items.name: Flexible Jurid coupling
items.what: The rubber disc coupling on the propshaft.
items.why: A rubber part, so check it for cracks. Its washers and bolts are listed too.

items.name: Differential
items.what: The sealed type 14 HU hypoid final drive, filled for life.
items.why: SNG sells the full unit only through the sales desk, but lists seals and bearings.

items.name: Differential output shaft
items.what: The short shaft each side of the diff that carries the driveshaft.
items.why: Bearings and seal renewed together. Output flange studs are JLM624.

items.name: Half shaft
items.what: The shaft from each diff output to the rear hub.
items.why: Same on both sides. Selective spacers are listed at this joint.

items.name: Universal joint
items.what: The joint at each end of the half shafts.
items.why: Four per car. Check for play.
items.location: Each end of each half shaft.

items.name: Half shaft spacer
items.what: A selective shim at the half shaft flange.
items.why: Available in 0.5 mm steps.
items.note: Only ends and midpoint are stored. Range runs CBC480635 to CBC480675 in the catalogue.

items.name: Front crossbeam
items.what: The aluminium casting bolted at four points to the longitudinals, carrying the suspension, rack and engine mounts.
items.why: Do not weld it, repair it or jack on it. Jaguar says a damaged beam must be replaced.
items.location: Under the engine, across the car.
items.accessNotes: Pressed-in bushes at the front, bolted mountings at the rear.

partNumbers.desc: Mounting bracket, to VIN A11050, qty 2
Mounting bracket RH, from VIN A11051
Mounting bracket LH, from VIN A11051

items.name: Vee mounting
items.what: The bolted rubber mounting at the rear of the crossbeam.
items.why: Two per car. Inspect the rubber for splits.
items.location: Under the ends of the front crossbeam.

items.name: Front subframe bush
items.what: The bush pressed into the front of the crossbeam.
items.why: Check with a pry bar at each inspection.

items.name: Upper wishbone
items.what: The one-piece forged steel upper arm, with a press-fit ball joint and two slipflex bushes per arm.
items.why: Caster is set by moving shims between front and rear of its fulcrum bolt. Note their position before removal.
items.accessNotes: Fulcrum shaft MJA1455AD on washers CAC3533 and nut JFX1160E. Shims MJA1467AA and MJA1467BA.

items.name: Upper wishbone bush
items.what: The rubber bushes in the inner ends of the upper arm.
items.why: Four needed. These tear with age.

items.name: Upper ball joint
items.what: The joint between upper wishbone and vertical link.
items.why: Press-fit in the wishbone, with its own lock nut.

partNumbers.desc: Upper ball joint lock nut, qty 2

items.name: Lower ball joint
items.what: The joint between lower wishbone and vertical link.
items.why: Nut JFX11205E is listed but the joint is not, as it comes with the arm in the catalogue.
items.location: Outer end of the lower arm.
items.note: No separate lower ball joint part number found.

items.name: Lower wishbone arm, front
items.what: The front half of the two-piece lower wishbone.
items.why: Sold as an assembly. Same on both sides.

partNumbers.desc: Lower wishbone arm, front, assembly, qty 2

items.name: Lower wishbone arm, rear
items.what: The rear half of the two-piece lower wishbone.
items.why: Side specific. Its eccentric bolt sets geometry.

partNumbers.desc: Eccentric shank bolt M12 x 105mm, qty 2

items.name: Vertical link
items.what: The upright that swivels on both ball joints and carries the hub, bearing, caliper and steering arm.
items.why: Standard and R-performance links differ, with a VIN break.
items.note: VIN A2290 reads as a shortened number; check against A22190, the R-performance break on the rear page.

items.name: Front wheel hub
items.what: The hub that carries the wheel and disc on the bearing.
items.why: Number changes at VIN 031303, the same point the disc size moves up. Brembo cars use their own hub.

items.name: Front wheel bearing
items.what: The cartridge bearing, greased for life, sealed and not adjustable.
items.why: Held by circlips with a VIN split, and the sensor rotor needs a special socket.

items.name: ABS sensor rotor
items.what: The hub rotor nut, a combined hub nut and ABS rotor.
items.why: Needs a special socket, sold by SNG, to take it off.

items.name: Front road spring
items.what: The coil spring that carries each front corner.
items.why: Springs come in several ratings by suspension spec, and that also sets the packers. Sold as a kit per axle.

4.0 supercharged coupe, adaptive; from A30645 coupe not R

items.what: The whole spring and damper unit, removed as one.
items.why: The unit you pull out to change either part.

items.why: R-performance cars use a different bar and bushes.

items.what: The rubber bush holding the bar to the crossbeam.
items.why: A cheap fix for clonks. SNG sells a Polybush version.

items.name: Front anti-roll bar link
items.what: The drop link from bar to lower arm.
items.why: Common source of front knocks.

items.name: Rear subframe
items.what: The frame that carries the differential, suspension and exhaust clearance.
items.why: The workshop manual contents list rear suspension and axle assembly removal as one job.

items.what: The hub that takes the wheel and the half shaft.
items.why: Number changes at VIN A18552. Wheel studs change type at A30645.

items.name: Rear hub bearing

items.name: Rear road spring
items.what: The coil spring on each rear damper.
items.why: Kit number depends on damping type and body.

items.why: Unit to remove when changing either part.

gaps: Factory text came from the JTIS 2.1 service manual and Jaguar Technical Guides already extracted on disk by the torques agent. The JTIS text carries specification tables and procedures, but no parts catalogue, so part numbers remain vendor sourced (SNG Barratt) and carry conf single unless cross-checked. Jaguar Club hosts the 1998 factory parts catalogue behind a member login, which was not used.

Connecting rod length: not found. Tried JTIS 2.1 engine sections, the AJ-V8 Technical Guide, XK8 guides, SAE 970914 (paywalled), Wikipedia and piston vendors. conrod.dimensions.rodLengthMm is null. Rod length needs a physical measurement or the SAE paper.

Timing chain pitch and link count: not found in JTIS, the guides or vendor pages. Autodoc refused automated fetch. JTIS confirms single-row primary chains on the 4.0 and multi-row on the 4.2. Seller pages mention 6.35 mm and 8.0 mm with no part tie, so pitch stays null.
Piston compression height and pin diameter: not found.
Road spring free length and rate: not found. JTIS says only that ratings vary by suspension spec, so dampers carry Bilstein lengths and springs carry ride heights.

Bearing sizes: front wheel bearing bore and outside diameter unconfirmed (one listing says 80 mm for MNC1830AA and 76 mm for MJA1830AE). No sizes found for rear CAC4610, CAC6333 or universal joint JLM1388.
Oil filter and fuel filter dimensions: not found for EAZ1354, C2C41611 or C2C35417. Cross-reference to Mahle OC 271 could not be confirmed. Web search budget ran out before more vendor lookups.

Part numbers with no catalogue line: engine.main-bearings, engine.piston, engine.exhaust-camshaft, front-suspension.spring-damper, rear-suspension.spring-damper, steering.wheel, wheels.tyre, electrical.gem, electrical.fusebox, body.shell, engine.camshaft-bearing-cap, engine.oil-separator, engine.oil-temperature-sensor, engine.piston-cooling-jet, rear-suspension.a-frame, rear-suspension.wide-mounting-frame, rear-suspension.monostrut, rear-suspension.tie-rod, driveline.propshaft-centre-bearing, exhaust.cradle, brakes.wheel-speed-sensor, cooling.filler-plug, fuel.purge-valve, fuel.carbon-canister, interior.seat-belt, interior.seat-belt-pretensioner, wheels.wheel-nut, induction.supercharger-coupler, interior.door-casing, interior.rear-seat-cushion, interior.rear-quarter-casing.

Exhaust camshaft, lower ball joint, 4.0 downpipes, ECM, 4.0 TCM, BPM, seats, wood fascia, steering wheel, pistons and main shells are sold by SNG through the sales desk or by VIN with no printed number. ECM, BPM and security module numbers shown come from used-market listings and only prove those cars.
Location is null on 40 parts and accessNotes is null on 289 parts, because no source was read for them. jobs.json is the place for procedure.
Fasteners, jobs and faults are filled from torques.json, jobs.json and faults.json after all references were normalised. tools/validate-data.mjs checks they stay in step.

All part references in other files now resolve to ids here. Sub-parts that had been folded into a parent (seals, gaskets, plugs, ducts, wheels by axle) are now real records with connectsTo pointing at the parent, so job parts lists and the 3D view do not lift the wrong thing. Part numbers moved to them from the parent where the catalogue line clearly matched.

Catalogue misprints are recorded in note fields rather than silently corrected. Examples: 2C2A1012, A415575, VIN 031202, A26998, MJF77440AA, A302645, GJA17310AD, and JLM21109 printed for both a brake booster and a gearbox connector.
Applicability by engine number break is kept in partNumbers.desc, as appliesTo has no engine number key.
Sample only lists: tappet shims, half shaft spacers, rear hub spacers, brake pipes and road wheels store representative numbers. See note on each record.
Thermostat opening temperature: seller listings disagree, 87 C versus 81 C, with no Jaguar figure in the sections read. 140 A for C2C19630 and 9 teeth on the starter are aftermarket figures.

Rear suspension naming: JTIS uses A frame, wide mounting frame, monostrut and wishbone tie, while SNG lists rear subframe, extension bracket and mounting bracket.
